result.title: NANO: Unifying Missingness and Input Uncertainty in Tabular Learning
result.summary: Missing values are common in tabular data, yet current approaches to handling them often overlook two dimensions. First, an observed value may be uncertain, while a Not-Observed (N.O.) value may still have a reasonable estimate. Inputs should therefore span a continuous spectrum from no evidence to a fully trusted observation. Second, Not-Applicable (N.A.) means that no meaningful value exists for a record, yet this semantic state often lacks explicit representation. To address both dimensions, we introduce NANO, a unified plug-in for input encoding that fits most token-based architectures. Guided by Bayesian evidence weighting, NANO adjusts the influence of a supplied value according to confidence, with all zero-confidence estimates mapped to the same N.O. representation. NANO accepts, but does not require, per-example confidence information during training or inference. For N.A., a separate representation enables models to encode inapplicability and its schema-defined reasons into context. Experiments across eleven datasets and nine backbones show that mixed-confidence training enables a single NANO model to generalize across inference confidence levels, remaining competitive without estimates and improving steadily as estimate reliability and confidence increase. The effectiveness of NANO's handling of N.A. is further demonstrated on three augmented datasets.

AI.brief_summary: 论文面向表格数据，提出 NANO 输入编码插件：以 Bayesian evidence weighting 按置信度缩放所给数值的影响，将所有零置信估计映射到同一「未观测」表示，并为「不适用」及原因设置独立表示；在 11 个数据集、9 个骨干网络上验证混合置信度训练可跨推理置信水平泛化。
AI.relevance_reason: 按置信度调节输入证据权重、把零置信证据归入统一空观测状态的思路，可能与 LVR 中视觉证据可靠性筛选及「无证据/不可用」状态表示相关，值得核查能否迁移到多模态输入的证据门控。
